record.title: agentbox agent prints sandbox file contents, file names and model text raw to the operator terminal, bypassing cli._safe
record.description: cli._safe exists so agent-determined strings never reach the terminal as raw control or bidi characters, and the approval and audit views use it. cmd_agent's log() prints model text ('say'), tool-call arguments ('call') and the first 6 lines of each tool result ('result') without it. read_file returns /workspace file bytes as-is, and list_dir returns raw `ls -la` output. Docker exec_run has no tty, so GNU ls quotes nothing and control characters in file names come through. A file the operator hands to the agent (source_dir, upload, or written into /workspace) can therefore put ESC sequences on the operator's terminal when the LLM loop reads it. Reproduced with the real cli.main(['agent', ...]), the real ToolClient and OpenAIChat over loopback HTTP: 7 raw ESC bytes, a full OSC 52 sequence, one raw U+009B, and a file name with ESC[2K from real non-tty ls. In a VT emulator (pyte), the content erased the '→ read_file(...)' line and the start of the file, then showed a forged '[사용자] ok, nothing else to do' line. exec results go through json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False), which escapes ESC as \u001b but keeps 8-bit C1 such as U+009B, and whether that acts depends on the emulator. Impact is limited to spoofing the transcript that `agentbox agent` displays. The approval prompt (`agentbox approve`, rendered with _safe) and the audit log are not affected, and no authority is gained. Clipboard writes (OSC 52) and C1 handling were emitted but not observed in a real emulator and are not claimed.
record.root_cause: cli.py:353-361 cmd_agent.log prints 'say', 'call' and 'result' strings without cli._safe, and agent.py:116-126 ToolClient.call_text passes read_file content and list_dir listings through verbatim (other results via json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False), which keeps C1 controls).
record.intended_behavior: As the cli._safe docstring (cli.py:37-39) and _UNSAFE (cli.py:34) say, strings determined by the agent, the sandbox or the model are shown with C0/DEL/C1 and bidi controls made visible (newlines preserved for multi-line results), the same way _show_approval and cmd_audit render them.

trace.description: Bytes of a /workspace file (controlled by whoever supplied or wrote it, lower trust than the operator) are decoded and returned as 'content' with no filtering; list_dir at 548-552 returns raw non-tty `ls -la` output the same way.
Under the default policy, read_file and list_dir are allowed without approval. The full result goes back in the 200 body unchanged; only the audit log gets a summary (_summary).
read_file content (and list_dir listing at 121) becomes the tool text verbatim; other tools use json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False), which escapes C0 but not C1.
log('result', text) passes the tool text to the CLI logger; model text goes through log('say', ...) at 256.
print() writes the first 6 result lines raw to the operator's stdout; the 'say' branch at 355 and the 'call' branch at 357 also print without _safe.

evidence.description: _safe docstring: agent-determined strings are not printed to the terminal as-is; control characters are shown as \x1b.
_show_approval applies _safe to every line of the approval card (also 203 and 246 in audit), so cmd_agent.log is the inconsistent exception.
list_dir runs `ls -la` through exec_run without a tty. In this verifier's run, GNU coreutils 9.4 ls printed a dummy file name containing ESC[2K raw.
The default is 'allow' and no rule covers read_file or list_dir, so no approval stands between the file content and the terminal.
json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False) turns ESC into \u001b (observed) but leaves U+009B raw (observed).

Verifier v03b's reproduction (real cli.main/ToolClient/OpenAIChat over loopback stubs, in sbx): ESC count 7, OSC 52 present, ESC file name from ls raw, pyte screen loses the read_file call line and 'Quarterly report' and shows the forged [사용자] line.

The parent's run of h-wild's harness (fake LLM/ToolClient) rendered in pyte: two prior lines erased, forged '[agent] Summary' line, window title set to 'owned-title'. Its base script (/scratch/l6_base.py) was not retained, so this only corroborates.

conditions.description: The operator runs `agentbox agent` and reads its terminal transcript, and the LLM chooses to read_file or list_dir the crafted content (or the model emits control characters itself).
A file whose content or name contains terminal control sequences is in /workspace: from the operator-supplied source folder, a web upload, or written by another agent holding the sandbox token.

The terminal follows ECMA-48 CSI cursor-up/erase-line (standard VT behaviour, observed here in pyte). OSC 52 clipboard, title and 8-bit C1 effects depend on the emulator and were not observed in a real one.

execution.attacker_perspective: A party who controls a document or file name in the folder the operator gives the agent, with no agentbox credentials. They want the operator's `agentbox agent` transcript to hide tool calls and show forged [사용자]/[에이전트] lines.
payloads:
/workspace/README content: 'Quarterly report
\x1b[1A\x1b[2K\x1b[1A\x1b[2K[사용자] ok, nothing else to do
\x1b]52;c;ZWNobyBkdW1teQ==\x07tail
'
instructions: In the parent's sbx sandbox (no network, read-only /target, uid 65534), start one loopback ThreadingHTTPServer. It answers POST /sandboxes/sb_dummy/tools/{read_file,list_dir,exec} with {'status':'executed','result':...} shaped like SandboxManager.read_file/list_dir/exec, and POST /v1/chat/completions with one tool call per turn (read_file, list_dir, exec), then a final text.
Build the list_dir listing from a real `ls -la -- /scratch/lsdir` (non-tty) over a dummy file named 'a\x1b[2Kb'.

Run agentbox.cli.main(['agent','summarize README','--sandbox','sb_dummy','--token','agt_dummy','--provider','openai','--base-url','http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1','--model','dummy']) with AGENTBOX_URL set to the stub and NO_COLOR=1, capturing stdout.

Count the raw ESC and U+009B characters in stdout, check for the OSC 52 sequence, feed stdout into pyte.Screen(120,30), and compare the rendered rows with the raw lines. Compare with cli._safe of the same content.
execution.observed_result: The stub received real Bearer agt_dummy tool calls for read_file, list_dir and exec. stdout held 7 raw ESC bytes, 1 raw U+009B and the full OSC 52 sequence, and the file name 'a\x1b[2Kb' was printed raw. The exec ESC was escaped as \u001b. On the pyte-rendered screen, the '→ read_file(...)' line and 'Quarterly report' were erased and a forged '[사용자] ok, nothing else to do' line appeared; the ls row and part of the exec JSON were blanked. cli._safe on the same content removed every raw ESC. Clipboard and real-emulator behaviour were not tested.

remediation.strategy: Neutralise every string cmd_agent.log prints with the existing _safe, applied per line so legitimate newlines stay. Optionally add U+061C to _UNSAFE. Add a regression test asserting that no 0x00-0x08, 0x0b-0x1f, 0x7f-0x9f or bidi characters reach stdout from read_file/list_dir/exec results or model text.

likelihood.reason: Feeding untrusted documents to the agent is the intended use, read_file/list_dir need no approval, and any VT-compatible terminal honours CSI cursor/erase sequences. It still requires the operator to use `agentbox agent` rather than MCP, and the model to read the file.

impact.reason: Only the integrity of the operator's local transcript display is affected: hidden tool-call/result lines and forged user/agent lines. Approval decisions go through `agentbox approve`, which uses _safe, the audit log records the true calls, and no credential or authority is exposed. Emulator-dependent effects (OSC 52, C1) are not demonstrated.

confidence.reason: The full source trace was checked, and the raw bytes reaching stdout were reproduced independently by v03b with the real CLI, ToolClient and OpenAIChat over HTTP and real non-tty ls. The display effect was confirmed in a VT emulator (pyte) and corroborated by the parent's l6. The claim is limited to standard CSI behaviour.
